status.label: Design ready — needs approval
status.detail: FancyZones is not clamping the realized snapped window back inside the monitor work area after Windows enforces a minimum width.

next_action.label: Approve the design and build the fix
next_action.reason: Approve the post-placement work-area clamp design and add the oversized-right-zone regression before touching broader FancyZones snapping behavior.

design.root_cause: FancyZones snaps a window by computing a zone rect, passing it through AdjustRectForSizeWindowToRect, and then calling SizeWindowToRect. That path never validates the final realized window rect against the monitor work area after Windows enforces a resizable window's minimum tracking size. On right-edge zones, a window such as Steam/GOG can end up wider than the zone, keep the requested left edge, and spill its realized right edge off-screen.
evidence: The issue repro is specifically a window that cannot shrink enough horizontally, dropped into a right-hand zone, ending with its right edge beyond the monitor bounds.

src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/WindowUtils.cpp adjusts borders and non-resizable windows, but SizeWindowToRect never clamps the final window rectangle back inside the monitor work area after SetWindowPlacement.
Existing unit tests cover resizable vs non-resizable snapping in WorkArea.Spec.cpp, but there is no regression covering a resizable window whose minimum width is larger than the target zone.

affected_files.purpose: Clamp the realized snapped window rectangle back inside the monitor work area after Windows applies min-size constraints.
Keep the snap path using the clamped placement helper without changing zone-history behavior.
Add a regression for a right-edge zone and a window that reports a minimum width larger than the zone width.
Provide a custom test window proc/class for a synthetic window that returns a large WM_GETMINMAXINFO minimum width.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: SizeWindowToRect writes the requested placement twice but never checks whether the final realized rect overflowed the monitor after Windows enforced the window's minimum width.
implementation_steps.change: After the second SetWindowPlacement, read the actual window rect, compute the monitor work area with MonitorFromRect/GetMonitorInfo, and if the realized rect overflows right/left/top/bottom, shift the entire rect back inside the work area without shrinking it.
tests: Add a right-edge oversized-window regression in WorkArea.Spec.cpp.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Test windows use DefWindowProc and cannot report a custom minimum tracking width, so the existing test suite cannot reproduce the oversize-right-edge condition.
implementation_steps.change: Add a dedicated synthetic test window class or optional window proc path that handles WM_GETMINMAXINFO and reports a minimum width larger than a single grid-zone width.
tests: Use the custom mock class only in the new right-edge clamp regression.
Keep other FancyZones tests using the existing default mock window path.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Current tests assert that a resizable window takes on the zone rect, but they do not exercise the case where Windows expands the window beyond the zone due to minimum-width constraints.
implementation_steps.change: Add a regression that snaps the custom large-min-width window into a right-side grid zone and asserts the resulting rect stays fully within the work area while remaining at least the minimum width.
tests: Run the existing WorkArea snap tests for resizable and non-resizable windows.

verify: Build FancyZonesLib and the FancyZones unit tests with the repo build scripts.
Run the updated WorkArea.Spec tests, especially the new right-edge oversized-window case and the existing resizable/non-resizable snap tests.
Manual repro with Steam/GOG or another minimum-width window on the rightmost zone: confirm the window remains fully visible on-screen after snapping even if it cannot fit the zone width exactly.
Regression-check left-side and multi-zone snapping to ensure oversized windows are shifted, not arbitrarily resized smaller than their enforced minimums.
risks: Clamping after placement must preserve the final size Windows chose, or the fix could fight the app's minimum-width contract.
Monitor work-area clamping must respect taskbar insets and mixed-DPI monitor coordinates.
Oversized windows snapped to extremely small zones may overlap neighbouring zones more visibly, but remaining on-screen is preferable to clipping off-screen.
alternatives: Trying to predict the final width only from the target zone rect is brittle because different windows report different minimum-track sizes.
Blindly shrinking the window to the zone width would violate the target app's own sizing constraints.
Hard-coding a right-edge-only special case would miss top, bottom, and left overflow scenarios on unusual work-area geometries.
